messages:
ashok: heads up — noticed a perf regression on prod from last night's kernel-hint change, lots of soft-429s on model-pool-a. p99 jumped ~210ms.
kevin: ugh. which hints landed? was that the new 'prefer-small-kernel' flag?
maria: yes, that was me. shipping that to reduce memory pressure for long-seq requests. did we test under our mixed workload?
ashok: payloads were similar to canary but real traffic mix is more short-chunk chat. batch formation slid to much smaller sizes and kv-hit-rate dropped 6%.
rajesh: kv-hit drop explains token cost increase but why soft-429s? batcher likely couldn't assemble target token budgets so admission started rejecting.
kevin: profiling from 02:00-03:00 shows continuous-batcher formed 70% micro-batches (<=2 reqs) vs baseline 28%. attached quick sample:

```
# batch-size distribution (sample)
baseline: 1:10% 2:18% 3:25% 4+:47%
after-hint: 1:34% 2:36% 3:20% 4+:10%
# avg kv-hit-rate: 0.82 -> 0.76
# p99 latency: 230ms -> 440ms
```

maria: hmm — kernel choice decreased per-token exec time for long sequences but small seqs lost benefit due to kernel switch overhead + more context swaps.
ashok: also saw queue-admit logic firing earlier because token-budget targets per-batch were miscalculated. the admit window uses expected batch tokens, which dropped, so token-lease accounting started throttling.
ops-jen: SLO alarms tripped at 02:12 — triggered auto-rollout pause. SRE-bot posted the incident summary.
sre-bot: incident (auto): increased soft-429s on model-pool-a, rolling back canary paused.
rajesh: root cause theory: kernel-hint heuristic changed kernel selection threshold so small requests prefer a kernel optimized for long sequences, which increases per-inference setup and reduces effective batching. this cascades to lower kv cache locality and smaller batches -> more 429s.
kevin: reproduction steps I used locally: run 1000 mixed chat requests (avg len 12 tokens, 60% short <8) against kernel-branch and main. attach script:

```
python perf/load_gen.py --profile mixed_short_long --concurrency 50 --duration 600 --target model-pool-a
```

maria: immediate mitigations: revert kernel-hint flag on model-pool-a, increase admit token-budget by 20% to give batcher a bit more headroom, and add a temporary exception rule for short-chat traffic routing.
ashok: for longer-term: we should make batching heuristics kernel-aware — prefer kernels that minimize batch-assembly overhead for the observed sequence-length distribution. and add a fast-path that keeps a small warm pool of short-seq kernels to avoid context swap costs.
rajesh: also add an observability metric: "kernel-switch-frequency" per-request so we can correlate switch churn with kv-hit and batch sizes.
kevin: I can add a quick patch to admit logic: when observed avg batch size < target for >2 minutes, auto-relax token_budget by +15% until stable. worth a canary?
ops-jen: let's open a short-lived rollback PR now and schedule a postmortem meeting tomorrow. action items in thread.
maria: patch ready for rollback: #PR 4321. test run on staging looks good. rolling now. :thumbsup:
ashok: thanks. postmortem agenda: timeline, kernel-hint test gaps, batching-admit coupling, KV-cache regression root cause, follow-ups (kernel-aware batching + token-budget auto-tuner).
kevin: I'll prepare perf graphs and a short sim that shows how batch assembler behaves under different kernel-selection heuristics.
rajesh: I'll prototype kernel-switch-frequency metric and add it to the console dashboard.
ops-jen: noted. scheduling postmortem at 10:00 UTC tomorrow and will include release owner and SRE.
maria: sorry for the churn — I'll add broader mixed-workload tests to the kernel hint PR checklist.
kevin: no worries — this is exactly why canaries exist. good catch, team.
